title: Bass Museum Expansion Plans
igCaption:
The Bass has expansion plans in Miami Beach.

Sources: Artforum, Dezeen, The Architect’s Newspaper, ArchDaily, Wikipedia

#MiamiBeach #TheBass #MiamiArt #SouthFlorida

scenes.text: Miami Beach’s Bass Museum just unveiled expansion plans. Voters already authorized $20.1 million for a new wing.
The Bass sits in Collins Park in Miami Beach. The museum was founded in 1963 and opened on April 7, 1964, inside the former Miami Beach Public Library.
scenes.caption: The Bass sits in Collins Park in Miami Beach. The museum was founded in 1963 and opened on April 7, 1964, inside the former Miami Beach Public Library.

scenes.text: John Bass and Johanna Redlich gave the city more than 500 works in 1963. The agreement required a Bass Museum of Art to stay open to the public in perpetuity.
scenes.caption: John Bass and Johanna Redlich gave the city more than 500 works in 1963. The agreement required a Bass Museum of Art to stay open to the public in perpetuity.

scenes.text: The building has changed before. A 16,000 square foot expansion designed by Arata Isozaki opened in 2002. The museum closed again in May 2015 and reopened on October 29, 2017.
scenes.caption: The building has changed before. A 16,000 sq ft expansion designed by Arata Isozaki opened in 2002. The museum closed again in May 2015 and reopened on October 29, 2017.

scenes.text: Johnston Marklee has unveiled designs for the next expansion. The firm will design a new pavilion for the campus expansion in Collins Park, and city-issued bond funds will add more exhibition space.
scenes.caption: Johnston Marklee has unveiled designs for the next expansion. The firm will design a new pavilion for the campus expansion in Collins Park, and city-issued bond funds will add more exhibition space.

scenes.text: Would you go more often if The Bass adds more exhibition space? It’s the same way you can leave a museum with a whole experience and still not know the person you kept passing by, which is what NEAR makes clearer.
